ratification.requested: The fix round asks the orchestrator to ratify a second clause on D15's renewal rule: the op key also renews when a selected entry's own match_history moves (a match landing or an existing one being unmatched), in addition to the brief's literal WHAT-changed enumeration (line ids, entry ids, cents).
ratification.brief_text_confirmed: brief-657.md:243-246 (§3 web item 5) enumerates only the WHAT-changed clause and says 'it renews on nothing else' — the fix's second clause is genuinely outside that literal text, correctly flagged rather than silently shipped.
ratification.reasoning: The amendment keeps D15's actual principle (the key is derived from a property of the DATA, never a component's lifecycle — entryGeneration reads match_history off the wire, is never sent to the door, and _reserve_op still re-hashes the real arguments). It is the minimal fix for a measured, reproducible blocker (SP1/A1): without it, match->unmatch->resubmit-identical silently tells a human a match landed while the line is still on the unmatched report — worse than widening one sentence in a brief. The residual (a concurrent unmatch between the last candidate read and the submit can still replay) is disclosed in the module header rather than hidden, which is the right way to carry a known gap forward. Recalled precedent, not evidence: this is the same shape as an HTTP conditional request's ETag/If-Match — a decision key derived from the resource's own current state so a stale intent cannot silently replay against a resource that has since changed; I know this pattern generally but cannot point to a specific Clara precedent for it, so it is offered as an argument, not a fact about this codebase. The orchestrator-supplied ruling for this session ('D14/D15 stand') does not name this specific clause, so it should not be read as a rejection; I recommend it be read into brief-657.md §3 item 5 and DECISIONS.md's D15 row explicitly rather than left as a comment-only amendment.
